text: Yeasts eat the lactic acid on the surface of the quark loaf and raise its pH; only then can the smear bacteria grow and give the yellow or red rind and strong smell.

sources.text: The table, the facts and the words on how it is made, from these.

steps.note: Sodium bicarbonate (Natron) or calcium carbonate is added, which takes up part of the acid.
steps.what: salt, spices (caraway) and a ripening agent

steps.note: The curd is shaped into small loaves.
The loaves are kept a few days, warm and very humid, with the film yeasts coming first.
The surface of the loaf is given salted water and red cultures.
The loaves are kept a few more days, cooler than before.

processing.text: The quark is sweated a few days warm and very humid, smeared with salted water and red cultures and kept cooler a few more days. Mould sorts are ripened 6-7 days at 17-19 °C.
